title: Concurrent catalog writes deadlocked: replicas ran the transaction observers in opposite orders
summary: From 00:20Z on 2026-10-31, concurrent resource permission creates of one product failed on dev anchor with `pq: deadlock detected (40P01)` and a 500. Three of four anchor post-deploy gates failed (`anchor: roles`, `anchor: resource-permission`), which held two merges off prod, while one gate passed and promoted the latent bug to prod. Since #309, a catalog write runs two in-transaction observers that take locks: the authz sync marker locks the product's `authz_sync_marks` row and the model size guard takes a product advisory lock. fx hands that observer group over in a random order per process, and dev and prod run two replicas, so each deploy has about one chance in two of opposite orders, and then concurrent writes deadlock. anchor#314 makes the emitter run observers in type-name order on every replica; it was live on dev at 05:51Z and on prod at 05:54Z. Prod logged no deadlock: nothing wrote its catalog concurrently.

impact.text: Dev: concurrent permission creates of one product answered 500 after about 1 s (Postgres deadlock_timeout). The anchor post-deploy gate failed on three deploys and held anchor#313 (Go SDK) and anchor#308 (log level) off prod. Prod ran the same code from 21:43Z on 2026-10-30, with two replicas whose order is unknown after its 02:25Z restart; VictoriaLogs shows no prod deadlock, so no customer request is known to have failed.

trigger: The 00:14Z dev deploy of anchor 7c4e3e55 (#310/#311) restarted both dev replicas. Each drew a new observer order, and the two came out opposite. The latent cause shipped with #309 at 21:40Z the day before, on a deploy whose replicas happened to agree.
detection: The 00:23Z post-deploy gate failed and the deploy-failure alert fired, as it did again at 02:59Z and 03:10Z, at night with nobody watching. The 05:08Z echopoint-investigation run reproduced the failure, isolated it with a 4-writer flow (serial creates 100 ms, concurrent 1.08 s and a 500), and found `deadlock detected (40P01)` on both dev replicas in VictoriaLogs.
resolution: anchor#314 sorts the observers by type name in `events.NewEmitter`, so every replica takes the mark-row lock before the advisory lock. A unit test proves that two group orders run the same order, and a CT races 8 distinct-name creates over 5 rounds. The fix went live on dev at 05:51Z; the gate was green at 05:52Z and the fix reached prod at 05:54Z. On dev, the 4-writer repro flow passed 3× and the `roles` and `resource-permission` flows passed.

whys.problem: Concurrent permission creates of one product answered 500 on dev, and the anchor deploy gate failed on 3 of 4 deploys

because.text: Postgres aborted one transaction per cycle with `deadlock detected (40P01)` after its 1 s deadlock_timeout
because.evidence: VictoriaLogs: 28 dev rows `pq: deadlock detected (40P01)` on POST /resource-permissions; repro flow: serial 100 ms, concurrent 1.08 s, one 500

because.text: Two transactions took the product's mark-row lock and its advisory lock in opposite orders
because.evidence: `fgasync.Marker` upserts `authz_sync_marks` (WholeProduct); `ModelSizeGuard` runs `pg_advisory_xact_lock(authz-model-size:<product>)`; deadlocks on replica .1 and .2 at the same second

because.text: Each replica ran the event observers in the order fx gave the `event_tx_observers` group, which dig shuffles per process
because.evidence: dig v1.19.0 `scope.go:109` seeds with time.Now, `shuffledCopy`; `events.NewEmitter` kept the slice as given; anchor runs 2 replicas (`NANOSTACK_REPLICAS=2`)

because.text: The emitter took the order of lock-taking observers from a container that defines no order
#309 added a second lock to the observer chain, and nothing stated the order observers lock in
because.evidence: `model_size.go` comment "It runs inside every write that emits an event"; agent-rules had no rule on observer locks

because.text: Every test runs Anchor in one process, so only one order ever ran against a database before deploy
because.evidence: TestConcurrentCatalogWritesOfOneProductAllSucceed passes on the unfixed code locally

because.text: The TxObserver contract said nothing about order or locks, and no test ran two orders
The bug reached prod, and the dev failure lasted five hours
The 02:24Z gate passed on a deploy whose replicas agreed and promoted 2774cf49
because.evidence: infra run 41159637931: suite success, prod deploy 02:25:39Z

because.text: Each deploy draws the order again, so the bug fails about half the gates, and a pass after failures reads as a flake
The gate promotes on one green run and ignores the same flow failing on the previous deploys
Three deploy-failure alerts between 00:23Z and 03:10Z had no reader until the 05:08Z routine
No routine reads the infra gate results; the suite routine only ran its own suite

contributing: The flows race their permission creates on purpose (sibling nodes); a serial graph would have hidden the deadlock.
PostHog no longer receives logs since infra#259 (2026-10-27); the first log search there found nothing, and VictoriaLogs held the 40P01 rows.

well: The flow suite's sibling creates sample races, and caught a cross-replica deadlock that no single-process test can.
A 4-writer throwaway flow turned a gate failure into a timing signature (1 s = deadlock_timeout) within minutes.
wrong: A green gate after two red ones promoted the bug to prod.
Three alerts went unread for five hours.
lucky: No prod caller wrote one product's catalog concurrently, so no customer saw a 500.
The merges held off prod were an SDK change and a log level, not a fix someone waited for.

actions.what: Run event observers in type-name order in `events.NewEmitter`, with a unit test over both group orders
agent-rules line: an observer takes its locks in type-name order; CT racing 8 distinct-name catalog writes
flow-suite-testing lesson: a flow that fails on some deploys of unchanged code is a per-process or per-replica order bug, not a flake
Decide whether the gate holds promotion while the same flow failed on one of the last 3 deploys
echopoint-investigation reads Deploy Router gate failures since its last run, every run

messaging.internal: anchor dev deadlocked concurrent permission creates since 00:20Z (observer order differs per replica since #309). Gate failed 3/4 deploys; one pass promoted it to prod (no prod deadlock seen). Fix anchor#314.
messaging.external: None: no customer request is known to have failed.
